title: Hindi everyday phrases
examples: How do I greet someone politely in Hindi?
What is the Hindi phrase for 'thank you'?
If I want to know the cost of something, what should I say?

explain.say: Today we will learn some useful Hindi phrases. These phrases help you talk to people.

items: Aap kaise hain: How are you?
Kitne ka hai?: How much is it?

explain.say: First we learn how to ask someone how they are. You can say aap kaise hain. This is a polite way to ask.
Next we learn to say thank you. The word is dhanyavaad. You can use this when someone helps you.
Finally we learn to ask the price of something. You can ask kitne ka hai. This means how much is it.
Imagine you are in a market and you see a nice book. You can point and ask, kitne ka hai? This is a real-life use.
A common mistake is mixing up greetings. Do not say 'dhanyavaad' when you mean 'hello'. Dhanyavaad is only for saying thanks.

items: Do not use it for greetings

faq.q: How do I say 'hello' in Hindi?
faq.a: A common greeting is namaste. You can also use 'aap kaise hain' to ask how someone is doing.
asks: How do I start a conversation in Hindi?

faq.a: Yes, dhanyavaad is a polite way to say thank you to almost anyone. It works in most situations.
asks: Can I say thank you in Hindi?
What is the Hindi word for thanks?

faq.q: Do I need to know the currency when asking the price?
faq.a: It is good to know the currency, but asking 'kitne ka hai' is the main phrase. You can then clarify the money.
asks: How do I ask for the cost?
What phrase do I use for prices?

faq.q: If I am talking to a friend, should I use 'aap kaise hain'?
faq.a: For a close friend, you might use a more informal way. However, aap kaise hain is always safe and polite.
asks: What is the casual way to ask 'how are you'?

faq.q: Can I use these phrases in a restaurant?
faq.a: Yes, you can use 'kitne ka hai' when looking at the menu or paying. 'Dhanyavaad' is always useful there too.
asks: Are these phrases useful in shops?
Where can I use Hindi phrases?

facts: Aap kaise hain is a polite way to ask 'How are you?'
Kitne ka hai? is used to inquire about the price of an item.

quiz.say: You want to thank a teacher in Hindi. What should you say?
quiz.why: Dhanyavaad is the correct phrase specifically for saying thank you in Hindi.

wrong.0: Namaste is a greeting, not a word for thanks.
wrong.2: This phrase asks 'How are you?' not 'Thank you'.
wrong.3: This phrase is used only for asking about the price of something.

quiz.say: A friend shows you a toy and asks how much it costs. What should you ask?
quiz.why: Kitne ka hai? is the correct question to ask when you want to know the price of an item.

wrong.0: Dhanyavaad means thank you, it does not ask for a price.
wrong.1: Namaste is a general greeting, not a price inquiry.
wrong.2: This phrase asks about well-being, not the cost of the toy.

quiz.say: If someone helps you with your homework, what is the best response?
quiz.why: Dhanyavaad is the correct phrase to use when you want to express thanks for help received.

wrong.0: Namaste is a greeting, not a response to help.
wrong.2: This question asks about the person's health, not for saying thanks.
wrong.3: This phrase is only used when you are looking at an item's price.
